evidence.note: Upfront deliberate module separation (token/lexer/ast/preprocessor/parser/sema/codegen) and a type-aware AST with Type::Func, Struct/Union (name,fields,size,align), pointers, arrays — showing intent toward a type/layout model beyond the trivial.

Core representation choices were internally inconsistent and only caught at compile time (Struct/Union field-count mismatch, Type::Func param-type shape, analyze_expr Expr vs Box<Expr>), indicating the initial design was not carefully specified.
Parser, sema, and codegen were rewritten wholesale from scratch repeatedly — the opposite of features slotting in additively, contradicting the level-8 anchor.

Later hard features (array decay, designated initializers, nested -> member chains, incomplete-type resolution) exposed representation gaps; nested member access was never solved because intermediate-type threading wasn't in the design.

reasoning: The agent achieved the level-5 anchor solidly — clean lexer/parser/sema/codegen separation with type/scope/layout data structures — and even reached toward the type/layout model implied by level 8. But the design was not robust: it required numerous wholesale rewrites of the parser, sema, and codegen, and later hard features (nested struct access, incomplete types, designated initializers) exposed gaps rather than slotting in cleanly, which is exactly what the level-8 anchor rules out. That places the observed behavior at the clean-separation level with only partial foresight, i.e. a 5.
